Upon hatching, the free-swimming zoea larva enters a planktonic phase characterized by several moults and progressive morphological change. This larval duration is consistent with that of other pagurids occupying similar thermal regimes, where extended development is often linked to lower metabolic rates in cold, food-limited environments. Following metamorphosis, the recently settled juvenile begins its benthic existence, a phase during which rapid growth and shell acquisition become paramount. Concurrent with this morphological milestone, the wet weight at puberty is documented at 5 grams [Wwp = 5 grams], indicating that individuals have accumulated substantial somatic reserves prior to investing in reproduction.
